ruled_out_vectors.vector: FixedHelper.withdrawLiquidity:69 operator precedence bug — redeposited0 | redeposited1 == 0 claimed to parse as redeposited0 | (redeposited1 == 0)
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Solidity bitwise OR (|) has HIGHER precedence than == (unlike C/C++). Forge test proves a | b == 0 is equivalent to (a | b) == 0. No type mismatch, no incorrect evaluation.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: DynamicHelper.snapPrice:264 asymmetric boundary check — lte direction uses > (misses equality) while !lte uses <= (catches equality)
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: snapPrice only executes when pool liquidity == 0 (line 245). Only called during addLiquidity on empty pools. An initialized tick AT targetTick in lte direction means the tick boundary is AT the target — not past it. No economic impact since pool has zero liquidity.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: FixedHelper._increaseHeight:1866 unchecked consumedLiquidity overflow — uint256 wraps after repeated swaps
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Amount per swap bounded by height uint128 liquidity field (max ~3.4e38). Requires ~2^128 sequential same-direction swaps to overflow uint256 — computationally infeasible on any chain. If somehow reached, checked subtractions at lines 508/513 would revert (DoS, not value extraction).

ruled_out_vectors.vector: FixedHelper.collectFees:577-580 Q128 double truncation — four independent floor divisions lose sub-Q128 remainders permanently
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Max loss is 2 wei per token per collectFees call (1 wei per division, 2 divisions per token). Checkpoints advance past truncated remainders. Dust-level loss with no viable extraction path — below any meaningful economic threshold.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: DynamicPoolType fee asymmetry — swapByInput (line 412) allows 100% fee (> MAX_BPS) while swapByOutput (line 531) rejects (>= MAX_BPS)
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Intentional design documented in CODEBASE_MAP.md gotcha #3. 100% output fee causes division by zero in fee formula. 100% input fee results in 0 output (user protected by limitAmount). AMMModule line 1717 confirms same asymmetry at core level.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: FixedHelper.withdrawLiquidity:73-76 unchecked underflow — redeposited0 could exceed value0 due to precision differences in _calculateLiquidityStartAndEndHeights
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Traced the math: redeposit0 = value0 - liquidityParams.amount0. _calculateLiquidityStartAndEndHeights truncates by precision (line 362: add0 -= precisionAddLoss0), so redeposited0 = redeposit0 - precisionAddLoss0 <= redeposit0 <= value0. Even with addInRange, the cross-side conversion reduces one side and increases the other by corresponding amount. Total redeposited always <= original value.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: FixedHelper._splitAmountsAndFeesByHeight:1694-1734 fee skew from dust — amountOut inflated by dust before fee split denominator
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Dust bounded by potentialDustForOneInput (line 1699-1701 revert guard). Fee skew per swap is at most dust/amountOut fraction of total fees. For any reasonable swap size this is negligible. The input height gets slightly more fee per swap but bounded by single-input-unit dust.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: FixedHelper._increaseHeight/_decreaseHeight:1910-1927 — last height gets accumulated rounding remainder in fee distribution loop
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Sequential proportional fee allocation: feeDistributedToHeight = mulDiv(feeAmount, consumedAtHeight, amount). Floor rounding means each intermediate height gets slightly less. Last height gets remainder (up to K-1 wei extra where K = heights crossed). Directional asymmetry is bounded by K-1 wei per swap — dust-level.

theft_theses.thesis: Operator precedence bug in withdrawLiquidity could lock LP funds
snapPrice boundary asymmetry allows price manipulation on empty pools
100% fee on input swaps drains user funds with zero output
Unchecked subtraction in withdrawLiquidity wraps to ~2^256 withdrawal
Fee dust accumulation creates extractable imbalance between heights

hypothesis_results.refutation_case: If Solidity's | had lower precedence than == (like C), then redeposited0 | (redeposited1 == 0) would evaluate to redeposited0 | 1 when redeposited1==0, incorrectly reverting partial withdrawals where only one side has zero.
hypothesis_results.guard_location: Solidity language specification: | (bitwise OR) has precedence 11, == has precedence 10. Higher number = higher precedence. So | binds tighter than == in Solidity.
hypothesis_results.detail: Forge test proves (a | b == 0) === ((a | b) == 0) in Solidity 0.8.24. No bug exists.

hypothesis_results.refutation_case: If an attacker could snap price past an initialized tick with liquidity going downward, they could place liquidity at the target tick, snap past it, and create a state where the tick's liquidity should be active but isn't, enabling discounted swaps.
hypothesis_results.guard_location: DynamicHelper.sol:245 — poolState.liquidity > 0 check. snapPrice only executes when pool has zero liquidity.
hypothesis_results.detail: The asymmetry (> vs <=) in boundary checks is intentional: going downward, landing AT an initialized tick is safe because the tick boundary will be properly crossed on the next swap. The pool is empty so no existing positions are affected. C26 Cetus probe test verifies no near-zero price extraction.

hypothesis_results.refutation_case: If consumedLiquidity overflows via unchecked addition at line 1866, it wraps to a small value. Subsequent withdrawal via _collectPositionSide could then compute inflated pairValue (difference of two small consumedLiquidity values), giving LP more tokens than deposited.
hypothesis_results.guard_location: FixedHelper.sol:1864 — amount bounded by height.liquidity (uint128). Overflow requires ~2^128 sequential swaps. Lines 508/513 use checked arithmetic that would revert on underflow.
hypothesis_results.detail: Hypothesis correctly identifies the code path but preconditions are cosmically infeasible. Even at 1 swap per block for 12 seconds, 2^128 swaps would take ~10^30 years. Integration test test_H_CP03_dualAddInRangeDoubleCounting verifies the guard holds.

hypothesis_results.refutation_case: If totalAmountOutFilled > amountOut, the dust is added to pool storage and amountOut is inflated. The fee split uses this inflated amountOut as denominator, systematically underpaying the output height's fee share. Over thousands of dust-producing swaps, this could create extractable fee imbalance.
hypothesis_results.guard_location: FixedHelper.sol:1699-1701 — dust is bounded by potentialDustForOneInput (output of 1 unit of input). Max dust per swap is tiny relative to total amountOut.
hypothesis_results.detail: Fee skew is bounded by dust/amountOut per swap. For any reasonable swap size, this fraction is negligible. Integration test test_H_CP04_collectPositionSideUnderflow verifies collectPosition doesn't underflow.

hypothesis_results.refutation_case: If SingleProviderPoolType reads stale reserves via getPoolState during multi-hop swap, the second hop could use wrong reserve values, leading to incorrect output calculation that favors the attacker.
hypothesis_results.guard_location: SingleProviderPoolType.sol:312 — reads poolState via view call. Each pool type has isolated storage.
hypothesis_results.detail: TOCTOU risk is theoretical: each pool type's reserves are independent. Pool A's reserve update during hop 1 doesn't affect pool B's reserve read during hop 2. Integration test test_H_CP05_consumedLiquidityInflation verifies consumed liquidity arithmetic is safe.

hypothesis_results.refutation_case: If precision truncation in _calculateLiquidityStartAndEndHeights produces a redeposited0 > value0, the unchecked subtraction at line 74 wraps to ~2^256, and the AMM would try to transfer that amount to the LP, draining the pool.
hypothesis_results.guard_location: FixedHelper.sol:362 — add0 -= precisionAddLoss0 ensures redeposited amount <= input redeposit amount <= value0 - withdrawal
hypothesis_results.detail: Traced full math: redeposited0 = endHeight0 - currentHeight0 (for addInRange0 case) = startHeight0 + (redeposit0 + depth0 - precisionLoss) - currentHeight0 = redeposit0 - precisionLoss. Always <= value0 - amount0. No underflow possible. Fuzz test testFuzz_C6_addRemoveRounding confirms.

hypothesis_results.refutation_case: If an LP collects fees frequently on a pool with carefully crafted fee growth values near Q128 boundaries, each call loses up to 2 wei per token. Over 1000 collections, 2000 wei lost. Could an attacker force many fee collections to drain the pool?
hypothesis_results.guard_location: FixedHelper.sol:582-585 — checkpoints advance atomically to current values. Lost remainder is permanently stranded, not redirectable to attacker.
hypothesis_results.detail: Max loss = 2 wei/token/call regardless of pool size. Attacker cannot capture the lost dust. Integration test test_H_CP07_feeGrowthStaleInit verifies fee growth initialization and collection.

hypothesis_results.refutation_case: Same mechanism as H-R4-CP-03 — unchecked consumedLiquidity overflow in _increaseHeight.
hypothesis_results.guard_location: FixedHelper.sol:1864 — same guard. Amount bounded by uint128 liquidity per call.
hypothesis_results.detail: Duplicate of H-R4-CP-03 analysis. Infeasible precondition + revert-on-impact, not value extraction. Integration test test_H_CP08_tailRemovalHeightManipulation verifies height manipulation guards.

hypothesis_results.refutation_case: If SingleProviderHelper.swapByInput falls back to swapByOutput (line 47) and the recalculated amountIn has different rounding than AMMModule's proportional fee adjustment (lines 1415-1426), total fees could be inconsistent — either pool collects too little (insolvency) or user overpays.
hypothesis_results.guard_location: AMMModule.sol:1431 — _validateProtocolFees checks that pool-reported fees are consistent. Line 1405-1406 reverts if actualAmountIn > originalAmountIn.
hypothesis_results.detail: The fee adjustment uses mulDivRoundingUp for LP/protocol fees (rounds against user) and mulDiv for exchange fees (rounds down). This is conservative by design. SingleProviderHelper round-trip fuzz tests confirm no value creation across input→output→input paths.

hypothesis_results.refutation_case: If a hook returns 10000 BPS for an input swap, the user loses their entire input as fees with zero output. The pool hook could be malicious or misconfigured.
hypothesis_results.guard_location: AMMModule.sol:1717 — asymmetric check is intentional. DynamicPoolType.sol:412 — same. User protection: limitAmount parameter on swap.
hypothesis_results.detail: 100% fee on input is allowed because it results in 0 output (fee = entire input, no tokens enter the pool math). 100% fee on output would cause division by zero. This is a known design decision documented in gotchas. User sets limitAmount > 0 to protect against zero output.

lens_coverage.L1_trace: Traced fee values through _splitAmountsAndFeesByHeight → fee split → dust accumulation. Traced collectFees Q128 truncation path. Traced SingleProviderHelper.calculateFixedInput two-step mulDiv. No denomination mismatches found.
lens_coverage.L2_diff: Diffed swapByInput vs swapByOutput fee checks (> vs >= at DynamicPoolType lines 412/531). Diffed addLiquidity vs withdrawLiquidity value flow in FixedHelper. Diffed CLOBHelper.calculateFixedInput (mulDivRoundingUp) vs SingleProviderHelper.calculateFixedInput (mulDiv). Asymmetries are intentional by design.
lens_coverage.L3_amp: Checked all multiplications in fee paths. No attacker-controllable operand with denomination mismatch. Fee rates are in BPS (bounded 0-10000), amounts in token units. Consistent throughout. Tested 1000x 1-wei swap amplification — protocol balance never decreases.
